stem: Article XIII, Section 3 says "The State shall afford full protection to labor." Which workers does this protection cover?
choices: Only union members who work inside the country
Local and overseas, organized and unorganized
Only workers employed by the government
Only workers with regular, permanent jobs
answer: Local and overseas, organized and unorganized
hints: The word "full" in "full protection" is a clue about how wide the coverage is.
Read the words right after "labor" in Article XIII, Section 3. They name two pairs of groups.
Section 3 pairs workers by place (in the country or abroad) and by union membership (in a union or not). Pick the choice that includes both sides of each pair.

solution.methodName: Find the provision, then match the key words

steps.action: Find the rule: "The State shall afford full protection to labor, local and overseas, organized and unorganized."
steps.why: Local means working in the Philippines; overseas means working abroad. Organized means belonging to a labor union; unorganized means not.

steps.action: See that the section covers both sides of each pair.
steps.why: So no worker is left out because of where they work or whether they belong to a union.

steps.action: Note the rights the same section guarantees.
steps.why: Workers have the rights to "self-organization, collective bargaining and negotiations, and peaceful concerted activities, including the right to strike in accordance with law." They are also entitled to "security of tenure, humane conditions of work, and a living wage."

steps.action: The protection covers labor local and overseas, organized and unorganized.

trapNotes.Only union members who work inside the c: This leaves out overseas workers and workers without a union. Section 3 covers both.
trapNotes.Only workers employed by the government: Section 3 protects labor in general and speaks of the relations "between workers and employers." It is not limited to government workers.
trapNotes.Only workers with regular, permanent job: Section 3 sets no such limit. It protects labor "local and overseas, organized and unorganized."
